title: Vetala Story 20: The Prince Who Was a Donkey by Day
summary: The Vetala whispered: 'Listen, King, to the prince cursed to be an ass!'...
keywords: vetala story 20: the prince who was a donkey by day
full_text:
King Vikramaditya shouldered the corpse once more.

The Vetala whispered: 'Listen, King, to the prince cursed to be an ass!'

Prince Somadeva was cursed by a sage to wear the form of an ass by day and a prince by night. A virtuous princess married him, knowing his curse, and tended him faithfully in the stable.

One night, while the prince slept in his human form, the princess took the coarse donkey skin and burned it in the hearth, breaking the curse forever.

The Vetala asked: 'King Vikramaditya, what broke the curse—the fire that burned the skin, or the princess's patient love?'

Vikramaditya replied: 'Her patient love alone broke the curse. The fire burned only the outward hide; but unless she had demonstrated unwavering fidelity through trials, the magical release would have turned to ash.'

'True, O King!' chuckled the Vetala, and vanished into the tree.
moral: True devotion sees through the beastly disguise to the noble prince within.
